title: CHRISTMAS IN THE VILLAGE
full_story:
Families and community members are invited to celebrate the holiday season in downtown Louisville on Sunday as “Christmas in the Village” returns with a full schedule of free activities, local food vendors, and festive entertainment.

The event, which runs from 3:00 pm to 8:00 pm, transforms the downtown area around the courthouse and Village Hall into a winter wonderland featuring 28 different activity stops, crafts, and seasonal treats.

The centerpiece of the evening takes place at 6:00 pm with the official tree lighting ceremony and the arrival of Santa and Mrs. Claus.  Visitors can enjoy free horse-drawn carriage rides throughout the event from 3:00 pm to 8:00 pm, with a brief pause around 6:00 pm for Santa’s arrival.  The Full Armor Bell Choir will perform at the Veterans Tree at 4:00 pm and 5:00 pm.  Full Armor FFA students will also present a Live Nativity near Village Hall, alongside a Nativity Festival hosted at Louisville Baptist Church.  Wabash Communications is presenting holiday movie screenings with showtimes at 5:15 pm and 7:00 pm at Diamond Dons Laundry Mat.

Attendees can start at Holiday Headquarters to pick up maps and kids’ goodie bags before exploring dozens of free stations hosted by local businesses and civic groups, Children can enjoy free mini canvas painting at Zink’s Art Studio, face painting at the Old Soda Fountain, sand ornament making at the Clay County Extension, free reindeer games at Clay County State Bank, and make-and-take cookie kits courtesy of the Clay County Farm Bureau.  Mrs. Claus will appear at the Clay County GOP office from 3:00 pm to 5:30 pm, followed by the Grinch from 5:30 pm to 8:00 pm.  Additional character meet-and-greets will take place at Blaine Wilhour’s office and Fat Dad’s, which will feature Frozen characters.  Free s’more kits will be handed out to the first 200 participants at the S’more Station, alongside free kids’ meals at Cruz Restaurant, free Olaf sundaes at Fat Dad’s, and free popcorn, candy, and refreshments scattered across town.  Hungry visitors can also stop by local food trucks including Blaze & Glaze Pizza Co., Blue Bird Baked Goods, Kenzie’s Sweet Shop, KRAZY Snowcone, The Fair Lady, and Pop’s Pit BBQ.

title: CAR DEER ACCIDENT
full_story:
A rural Iuka man was injured Thursday evening after swerving his motorcycle to avoid a deer east of Salem.

Authorities say 20-year-old Carter Moore of Metcalf Road lost control of his bike on US 50 at Kinmundy Road around 5:19 pm, causing the motorcycle to overturn.

Moore took himself to the Salem Township Hospital emergency room for treatment.

title: BLOOD DRIVES
full_story:
Clay County residents have an upcoming opportunity to help save lives before the Thanksgiving Holiday.

The American Red Cross is teaming up with the Flora Chamber Of Commerce and Flora Odd Fellows Lodge number 151 for a pre-Thanksgiving blood drive.

The drive will be held Wednesday, from 1:00 to 5:00 pm at the Flora Odd Fellows Lodge, located at 231 East North Avenue in Flora.

Organizers note that the winter holidays often bring a drop in donations, making local drives essential for maintaining area blood supplies.  As an added incentive, those who come out to give blood on Wednesday will receive an exclusive American Red Cross and Wheel Of Fortune mug, while supplies last.

To donate, individuals must be at least 17 years old, weigh at least 110 pounds, and be in generally good health.  Donors are asked to bring a blood donor card, driver’s license, or two other forms of identification.

Appointments can be made using the Red Cross Blood Donor App, by visiting RedCrossBlood.org, by calling 1-800-RED CROSS or by enabling the Blood Donor Skill on Alexa Echo devices.  Donors can use RapidPass online on the day of their appointment to complete pre-donation reading and health history questionnaires before arriving.

There will be a Blood Drive on Tuesday, December 1st from Noon to 6 pm at the Blue Point Free Will Baptist Church in the Link Gymnasium.  The next Blood Drive at the Flora Church of the Nazarene will be on Thursday, December 10th from Noon to 5 pm.

title: NORTH CLAY BOARD
full_story:
The North Clay Unit 25 Board of Education approved a five-year contract extension for Superintendent Keith Price during its regular meeting Wednesday night in Louisville.

Following a closed session, the board voted six-to-zero to extend Price’s contract, along with hiring Dee Ann Hronec as a bus aide and Marisa Perry as a paraprofessional for the 2026-2027 school year.

In financial business, the board unanimously approved a tentative 2026 tax levy that represents a 4-point-99 percent increase over last year.  Price noted the levy could actually lower the district’s overall tax rate from 3.15 to somewhere between 3.11 and 3.03, depending on final equalized assessed values.

Board members also gave the green light to two campus construction projects.  The board approved plans for the FFA and FFA Alumni to build a 30-by-50-foot pavilion with attached storage north of the greenhouse, funded in part by the Cody Blair and Caide Weidner memorials.  They also approved a conceptual design for a new restroom and concession stand at the high school baseball field, opting for a layout modeled after the facility at the Flora Pickleball Court.

Additionally, the board approved the 2025-2026 school report cards.  Principal Ben Borries reported the Elementary and Junior High School achieved an “Approaching Exemplary” state rating, highlighted by a 95.8% student attendance rate and gains in English Language Arts and math.  High School Principal Sarah Newby reported a “Developing” state rating for the high school, noting growth in science proficiency and a 93.4% attendance rate.

Earlier in the meeting, the board recognized Junior High cross country runners Madi Sparks and Jazey Keller for qualifying for the state meet in Bloomington-Normal.

title: MEMORIAL HIGHWAY NAMED
full_story:
State Senator Terri Bryant and State Representative Dave Severin hosted a ceremony Friday, in Woodlawn to officially dedicate a stretch of Illinois Route 15 in memory of fallen Marine Lance Corporal J. Kyle Price.

The Illinois House and Senate approved HJR 62 in May 2026, renaming a stretch of Illinois Route 15 between Woodlawn and Mount Vernon the “Lance Corporal Jonathan Kyle Price Memorial Highway.”  Lance Corporal Price lost his life while serving our nation during a tour of duty in Iraq in January 2006.

Severin worked closely with Price’s family to draft the resolution honoring his memory and earned unanimous support from his House colleagues.  He says the Lance Corporal J. Kyle Price Memorial Highway will serve as a reminder to all of us who pass through it that our freedom isn’t free, and we owe a debt to our fallen heroes that we can never repay.

Bryant says she was honored to work alongside Severin in supporting Price’s family and friends in their efforts to secure the highway designation.

“Kyle Price’s memory has been kept alive for years by his friends and family, who have worked diligently to support a variety of charitable pursuits to benefit youth, military families, and veterans in our communities,” Bryant said.  “Renaming a road for a fallen hero is an appropriate and meaningful way of honoring Kyle’s service and ultimate sacrifice in defense of our nation.”

The ceremony took place along Illinois Route 15 just outside Woodlawn.

title: ICASH AUCTION
full_story:
If you’re looking for unique holiday gifts, the Illinois State Treasurer’s Office is kicking off an online unclaimed property auction.

Treasurer Michael Frerichs says the I-Cash auction runs through November 29th on the Hi-Bid website.

A total of 150 lots are up for grabs, featuring items surrendered to the state from unclaimed safe deposit boxes after sitting untouched for at least ten years.  Highlights include a Towle sterling silver cup, 14-karat gold pins, a 10-ounce fine silver bar, Morgan silver dollars from the late 1800s, and vintage basketball cards of NBA greats Michael Jordan and Penny Hardaway.

All proceeds from the sale will continue to be held by the state for the rightful owners, no matter how long it takes for them to come forward.

To view the catalog and place a bid, shoppers must create an account at Hi-Bid dot com.  Anyone with questions can call the Treasurer’s Office at 217-557-8567.  You can also check if the state is holding any missing money for you at I-Cash dot Illinois Treasurer dot gov.

title: CHRISTMAS OPEN HOUSE
full_story:
The Vandalia Statehouse State Historic Site, the oldest surviving state capitol building in Illinois, welcomes visitors for its annual Christmas open house and candlelight tours from 5 to 7 pm Saturday, December 12th.

Visitors can explore the historic building illuminated by more than 150 candles and decorated for the holiday season.  Guests can stroll through the Statehouse and enjoy the festive atmosphere while warming up with hot apple cider and cookies.

The first 100 families to attend will receive a free commemorative Christmas ornament.  Visitors are encouraged to bring nonperishable food items or canned goods to donate to a local food pantry.

The event is hosted by the Illinois Department of Natural Resources and the Old Capitol Foundation.  Admission is free, but donations to support the preservation and maintenance of the historic site are welcome.

The Vandalia Statehouse served as Illinois’ state Capitol from 1836 to 1839 and remains an important part of the state’s history.  Located at 315 W. Gallatin Street in Vandalia, the site is open to the public Wednesday through Sunday from 9 am to 4 pm.

For more information, call the Vandalia Statehouse State Historic Site at 618-283-1161.

title: EIU AWARDS BID
full_story:
Eastern Illinois University (EIU) reached a major milestone toward construction of its new Integrated Science Building, with the State of Illinois formally awarding the general construction contract for the project.

The Illinois Capital Development Board (CDB) issued a Notice of Award to Grunloh Construction, Inc., of Effingham, on Tuesday.  The $104.56 million contract follows the company’s successful bid in September and officially moves the project closer to construction.

The approximately 120,000-square-foot, three-story facility will replace outdated science spaces with modern classrooms, teaching laboratories and research facilities designed to support EIU’s growing academic needs.

Designed by RATIO Architects, the new building will bring several science disciplines together in a modern, integrated learning and research environment.  The facility will meet LEED Silver sustainability standards and include specialized laboratories, classrooms, faculty offices and student collaboration spaces.

The building’s three floors will be organized to support instruction, research and collaboration across multiple disciplines.  Biological Sciences will occupy portions of the first and second floors, alongside a new main lecture hall.  The second floor will also include Biochemistry teaching and research spaces, while the third floor will house Chemistry laboratories and a student work cafe.  Additional features will include modern teaching and research laboratories, expanded fume hood capacity, upgraded ventilation systems, hazardous waste management facilities, a cold room and dedicated spaces for student collaboration.

An official groundbreaking ceremony is anticipated on January 21st, with additional details to be announced as plans are finalized. The university’s strategic facilities planning targets a late 2029 opening for the new building.

title: FAMILY FARM PRESERVATION ACT
full_story:
Supporters of estate tax reform in Illinois are hoping the Family Farm Preservation Act can get to the finish line this year.  The legislation would raise the Illinois estate tax threshold from $4 million to $6 million and make it an exemption, not a threshold.  Only dollars over $6 million would be taxed, as opposed to the current law where the entire estate is taxed if the threshold is breached.  Mike Borgic is the Sangamon County Farm Bureau President.

The legislation would also tie the $6 million exemption to inflation.
